title: Benchmarking AI risk behaviors
abstract: arXiv:2611.16318v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We evaluate LLM risk propensities across a range of contexts and task demands. We evaluate models for how risk averse or risk tolerant they are in various conditions, as well as how stable and consistent their behavior is across conditions. We present a toolkit for developing model risk profiles that can be used to predict model behavior and which can be adapted to include new evaluations of risk propensities. We also examine how these properties have changed across model generations and families. We observe that 2026 state-of-the-art models tend to be more stable, more consistent, and more risk neutral than older models. These trends appear to be related; newer models are more stable and consistent because they are more likely to use expected value maximization as a decision procedure.

translated_abstract: 我们在一系列情境和任务需求下评估了大语言模型（LLM）的风险倾向。我们评估了模型在各种条件下对风险的厌恶或容忍程度，以及其行为在不同条件下的稳定性和一致性。我们提出了一个用于构建模型风险画像的工具包，该工具包可用于预测模型行为，并可扩展纳入新的风险倾向评估。我们还考察了这些特性在不同模型代际和模型家族之间的变化。我们观察到，2026年的最先进模型往往比旧模型更稳定、更一致，且更趋于风险中性。这些趋势似乎是相互关联的：较新的模型之所以更稳定、更一致，是因为它们更倾向于将期望值最大化作为决策程序。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个评估LLM风险倾向的工具包，发现2026年最先进模型因更倾向于采用期望值最大化作为决策程序，而比旧模型更稳定、更一致且更趋于风险中性。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a toolkit for profiling LLM risk propensities and finds that 2026 state-of-the-art models are more stable, consistent, and risk-neutral than older models because they increasingly adopt expected value maximization as a decision procedure.
